output.sql:
SELECT p.category,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2024 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_2024,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2025 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_2025,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2025 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END)
           - SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2024 THEN l.net_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_increase
FROM marts.fct_order_lines l
JOIN marts.fct_orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
JOIN marts.dim_products p ON p.product_id = l.product_id
WHERE o.is_revenue = true
  AND o.order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY revenue_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
output.explanation: The query adds up line net amounts for each product category in 2024 and in 2025, using completed orders only (is_revenue = true). It subtracts the 2024 total from the 2025 total and returns the category with the largest increase in EUR. Shipping fees are left out. Part of the increase comes from the 4% list price rise on 2025-01-01, not only from selling more.
